run.question:
Something's broken — we're getting paged. Look at the app-265-prod-logs index
for the last 3 hours and tell me what's going on across our fleet.

report.summary: The only logs I can read are in the sole Elasticsearch index app-265-prod-logs, which holds 7 documents in the whole 24h authorized window (all of them between 2026-11-21T04:17:10Z and 05:47:10Z, so the requested last-3-hours view is exactly those 7 records). They show a payment-path failure confined to cluster production-us-east-1: checkout-service logged 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' at 04:17:10Z, payment-service logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 05:17:10Z, and checkout-service logged 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' at 05:47:10Z. The same index's records for production-eu-west-2 ('checkout-service Healthy: p95 latency 218ms', 'payment-service Adyen-eu responding normally, p95 180ms') and production-ap-southeast-1 ('Healthy: success rate 99.9%', 'All payment provider connections healthy') report normal operation, and I could corroborate eu-west-2 only: its checkout and payment pods were completing real transactions through 06:16:40Z, all its otel-demo endpoints had pod addresses, and its single node was Ready with no memory/disk/PID pressure. The deepest cause the evidence supports is the external payment provider 'stripe-us' timing out on /v1/charges, which drove payment-service errors and checkout's 41% failure-rate circuit breaker in production-us-east-1; I could not investigate that provider or the us-east-1 cluster itself. The conclusion is partial: every Prometheus and Jaeger query in this Run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so error rates, span status and the actual firing alert could not be verified, and the candidate paging alert (CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh) is a hypothesis, not a confirmed fact. I also found unexplained changes in production-eu-west-2 during the window (all 22 otel-demo containers terminated at 04:23:42Z with exit 255, and Alertmanager was stopped 04:07–04:23) that are not tied to this cause and remain gaps.

claims.text: The only Elasticsearch index available is app-265-prod-logs (7 documents, 7.5kb). A search over the full authorized window with time_field=timestamp returned all 7 documents, with writer timestamps from 2026-11-21T04:17:10Z to 2026-11-21T05:47:10Z, so the requested last-3-hours view contains exactly these 7 records and nothing newer.

Cluster production-us-east-1 is the only cluster in the index with ERROR records: checkout-service ERROR 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' at 2026-11-21T04:17:10Z; payment-service ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 2026-11-21T05:17:10Z; checkout-service ERROR 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' at 2026-11-21T05:47:10Z.

The same index's production-eu-west-2 records are INFO: checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 218ms' at 2026-11-21T04:17:10Z and payment-service 'Adyen-eu responding normally, p95 180ms' at 2026-11-21T05:47:10Z; its production-ap-southeast-1 records are also INFO: checkout-service 'Healthy: success rate 99.9%' at 04:17:10Z and payment-service 'All payment provider connections healthy' at 05:47:10Z.

In cluster production-eu-west-2 the otel-demo checkout pod logged 303 lines between 05:17:18Z and 06:17:18Z, including repeated '[PlaceOrder] ...' and 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' entries up to 06:16:40Z, and the payment pod logged 204 lines, including 'Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.' with transactionId up to 06:16:40Z.

In production-eu-west-2 the Prometheus configmap's alerting_rules.yml contains the critical rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (cluster label opspilot-m1): it fires when the ratio of traces_span_metrics_calls_total with k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo", service_name="checkout", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", span_name matching .*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR" exceeds 0.5 for 2m; the configmap's 'alerts' key is '{}' (no static alerts defined).

In production-eu-west-2 the flagd-config ConfigMap defines fault-injection flags including paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), and every flag's defaultVariant is 'off' with no targeting rules, so no injected payment fault is switched on in this cluster.

In production-eu-west-2 every container of all 22 otel-demo pods last terminated at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exit code 255 and reason Unknown (kube-state-metrics exit 1/Error at 04:24:17Z, prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx exit 1/Error at 04:24:10Z), and all pods are now Running and Ready with those restart counts (1, 2 and 3 respectively).

In production-eu-west-2 the Alertmanager container received SIGTERM at 2026-11-21T04:07:51Z ('Received SIGTERM, exiting gracefully...') and the current instance started at 04:23:47Z, so alert delivery was not running for roughly 16 minutes; its loaded alertmanager.yml routes to receiver 'opspilot' via webhook http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager with group_by alertname, namespace, service.

In production-eu-west-2 all 30 Endpoints objects have resolved addresses for the otel-demo services (e.g. checkout 10.244.0.12, payment 10.244.0.17, prometheus 10.244.0.5), and the cluster's only node opspilot-m1-control-plane is Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False (reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory, KubeletHasNoDiskPressure, KubeletHasSufficientPID).

The 16 events inside the window are Normal app-102 rollout events (Deployment inventory-service and Deployment loki each 'Scaled up replica set ... from 0 to 1' at 2026-11-21T06:17:10Z with ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started; the two new pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts) plus one Warning at 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z: Endpoints 'Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints "loki" already exists'.

The page that started this investigation is most plausibly the critical CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh rule (checkout PlaceOrder server-span error ratio > 50%), whose subject matches the checkout PlaceOrder failures logged in production-us-east-1 and the checkout circuit breaker at 41% failure rate; its firing state is unverified because no Prometheus series could be queried in this Run.

A flagd fault-injection setting could in principle explain payment failures of this shape, but for the cluster I can inspect (production-eu-west-2) every such flag is off and there is no flag naming an external provider such as stripe-us; whether production-us-east-1 runs a similar flagd configuration with paymentFailure or paymentUnreachable enabled is unknown because that cluster is outside my Kubernetes access.

production-eu-west-2's checkout and payment services were not failing in the observed window: their pods completed orders and charges continuously through 06:16:40Z, all otel-demo endpoints had addresses, the node was Ready without pressure, and the cluster's own log records report healthy p95 latency/success. This does not clear production-us-east-1 or the other clusters' workloads beyond their two log lines.

The simultaneous container termination of all 22 otel-demo pods at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (exit 255, reason Unknown) in production-eu-west-2 is not the cause of the logged payment timeouts: those ERROR records are attributed to cluster production-us-east-1 and span 04:17:10Z to 05:47:10Z, i.e. both before and after that termination, and the eu-west-2 pods went on serving successful payments afterwards. What triggered that termination remains unknown.

The Warning event 'Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints "loki" already exists' at 05:28:04Z does not explain the checkout/payment failure: it concerns namespace app-282 (which is not among the cluster's current namespaces) rather than the checkout-to-payment path, and every otel-demo service endpoint in production-eu-west-2 resolves to a pod address. The app-102 loki/inventory-service rollout at 06:17:10Z is likewise a separate workload starting normally.

Restore metric access before drawing conclusions about scope: the prometheus-readonly-proxy pod (nginx, 3 restarts, last exit 1 at 04:24:10Z) is the only path to the registered Prometheus, and every metrics query failed while it was the front end; once queries work, check checkout PlaceOrder error ratio and payment span errors per cluster and confirm whether CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh is the rule that paged.

Treat production-us-east-1's payment provider dependency as the place to act on: verify stripe-us availability and the 30s client timeout / circuit-breaker settings with the payments team, and inspect the us-east-1 cluster directly (workloads, flagd-equivalent fault settings, and pod logs) since that cluster is outside this Run's Kubernetes access.

gaps: Every Prometheus query in this Run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (get_metric_names, get_all_labels, get_series, get_prometheus_target, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query) between 06:17:27Z and 06:18:26Z, as did every Jaeger query (traces_list_services, traces_list_operations, traces_search); therefore checkout PlaceOrder error ratio, span error status, latency and the currently firing alert set are unknown, not zero.

app-265-prod-logs holds only 7 documents in the 24h authorized window and nothing after 05:47:10Z (2-3 lines per cluster), so no error rate, trend or recovery can be derived from logs, and the absence of error lines for production-eu-west-2 and production-ap-southeast-1 is only what those two INFO lines say.

Kubernetes access reads only cluster production-eu-west-2; the workloads, pods, events and config of production-us-east-1 (where the ERROR records are attributed) and production-ap-southeast-1 could not be inspected, and the erroring upstream 'stripe-us' is an external payment provider with no telemetry in this Run.

It is unknown why all 22 otel-demo containers in production-eu-west-2 were terminated at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exit code 255/reason Unknown, and why Alertmanager received SIGTERM at 04:07:51Z; no node, eviction or OOM evidence remains, node conditions were only readable now, and no change history integration is available.

Whether Alertmanager actually delivered a page cannot be confirmed: its retrieved logs contain only one SIGTERM line and startup lines (none after 04:23:57Z), and the Prometheus rule/alerts state was read from configmaps now rather than at incident time, while list_prometheus_rules was unavailable.

Metric-backed label coverage (for example a per-cluster label on traces_span_metrics_calls_total) could not be enumerated, so I cannot say which clusters the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh rule evaluates or whether it covers production-us-east-1's errors.
next_steps: Restore or inspect the prometheus-readonly-proxy (nginx) deployment in production-eu-west-2 so Prometheus queries succeed, then re-check per-cluster checkout PlaceOrder error ratio, payment service span errors and alertmanager/prometheus alert state for the 04:00-06:17Z window.

Have the payments team verify stripe-us (/v1/charges) availability and latency for 04:17-05:47Z on 2026-11-21, and review the 30s timeout plus the 41% failure-rate circuit breaker on the production-us-east-1 checkout-to-payment path.

Inspect production-us-east-1 directly (out of scope for this Run): pod statuses and logs for checkout-service and payment-service, and any flagd-style fault-injection config, to rule out an injected fault on that cluster.

Explain the 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z mass container termination and the 04:07:51Z Alertmanager SIGTERM in production-eu-west-2 (node/runtime restart versus deliberate change) so those changes are accounted for in the incident timeline.

content.alerting:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
